reason: B is the stronger proposal because it defines a specific W–Ta–Cr–V baseline, irradiation window, measurable defect and hardening outcomes, and a decisive comparison, while its cited study directly supports Hf-modified quinary alloys in this regime. Its assumption of coherent Hf-rich precipitates still requires verification and may misstate the actual benefit of Hf, but A relies on uncontrolled oxygen to create Y oxides and provides no evidence that simple Y alloying will reproducibly yield a stable oxide dispersion without harming grain-boundary integrity.
